security_spec.violation_condition: In XiangShan RTL, when a CSR write (csrrw/csrrs/csrrc) targets the APLIC indirect access register xireg with xiselect set to access acliciprio[0] or aclicsourcecfg[0], the hardware writes the data value into the corresponding target[0] or sourcecfg[0] storage flop instead of forcing those bits/storage to zero and ignoring the write. Specifically: (1) xiselect=0x0000 accesses acliciprio[0] — the 8-bit field corresponding to target[0].iprio must be hardwired to read-as-zero and ignore writes, but the RTL may implement it as a writable register. (2) XLEN=32, xiselect=0x1000 accesses aclicsourcecfg[0] via xireg2 — the register must return zero and discard writes, but the RTL may instantiate it as a functional writable CSR slice mirroring a non-existent sourcecfg[0].
security_spec.summary: APLIC indirect CSR access to acliciprio[0] target[0] field and aclicsourcecfg[0] must be hardwired read-only-zero (ROZ) since APLIC domains do not implement target[0]; writable RTL implementation would allow software to configure a non-existent interrupt target, causing undefined interrupt routing behavior and potential privilege boundary violations.

findings.finding: No Smidctrl/Ssidctrl implementation exists in XiangShan RTL. There is no xiselect register, no xireg[4:6] accessor CSR, and no xacliciprio/xaclicsourcecfg storage array. The existing miselect/siselect/vsiselect WARL maxValue=0xFF/0xFFF prevents writing the APLIC 0x1000-0x10FF range. The violation condition (CSR write targeting xireg with xiselect=0x1000 setting target[0].iprio or sourcecfg[0]) cannot arise because the underlying hardware simply does not exist.
findings.snippet:
MISelectField: maxValue = 0xFF (line 225-231)
SISelectField: maxValue = 0xFFF (line 233-239)
VSISelectField: maxValue = 0xFFF (line 216-223)
isIllegal := value >= 0x100.U  // traps all values >= 0x100

spec_citations.excerpt: APLIC domains do not implement target[0]. When accessing acliciprio[0], the bits corresponding to target[0] are read-only zero.
Access to aclicsourcecfg[0][15:0] is read-only zero.
The registers xireg4 through xireg6 are reserved and raise an illegal instruction exception when xiselect is in the range 0x1000-0x10FF.

findings.finding: IndirectCSRPermitModule correctly traps all ireg[2:6] accesses (rwMireg2_6_EX_II, rwSireg2_6_EX_II, rwVSireg2_6_EX_II always true) and all ireg accesses with iselect outside AIA/IMSIC ranges via Iselect.isInOthers. Since no Smidctrl storage exists behind these CSR addresses, even if a write bypassed the trap logic, it would land on ZeroFieldBundle hardwired to 0.U (CSRIND.scala:17-90) — no writable flop exists to be corrupted.
findings.snippet:
rwMireg2_6_EX_II = Ireg.isInMireg2_6(addr)  // always traps
rwMireg_EX_II := (Iselect.isInAIA(miselect) && Iselect.isOdd(miselect) ||
  Iselect.isInOthers(miselect)) && addr === CSRs.mireg.U

findings.finding: All mireg2-6, sireg2-6, and vsireg2-6 CSR modules use ZeroFieldBundle hardwired to 0.U. These would be the xacliciprio and xaclicsourcecfg accessor registers under Smidctrl, but they are currently reserved with no writable storage. The ROZ constraint on target[0].iprio and sourcecfg[0] is vacuously satisfied because there is no target[0] or sourcecfg[0] to erroneously write to.

SISelectField/VSISelectField WARL legalRange maxValue=0xFFF permits values 0x100-0xFFF to be written and stored (isLegal returns true). These reserved values pass WARL but trap later on ireg access via IndirectCSRPermitModule. The two-layer enforcement (WARL accept + permit-module trap) is fragile: a future maintainer removing the permit-module trap without updating WARL ranges would silently allow invalid select values. Reserved subranges declared in Seq are documentation-only — not enforced in hardware. This is a latent risk distinct from the Smidctrl ROZ issue.

spec_citations.excerpt: The behavior upon accessing mireg* from M-mode, while miselect holds a value that is not implemented, is UNSPECIFIED.

findings.finding: The isIllegal output from miselect/siselect/vsiselect (declared in HasISelectBundle trait, CSRAIA.scala:18-25) is never consumed in NewCSR.scala. Grep confirms zero reads of isIllegal. The IndirectCSRPermitModule independently re-derives range classification via Iselect.isInAIA/isInImsic/isInOthers. This is orphaned dead code: a future maintainer fixing only isIllegal logic without updating the permit module would create a silent bypass. If Smidctrl is later implemented and isIllegal is wired up, inconsistency between the two range-check paths could allow xiselect=0x1000 to be stored while the permit module still traps or vice versa.
